HCI-Portrait Findings

Review the main findings, inspect activity-specific dimensions, and explore the seven producer configurations.

Interview guide

Move between findings and supporting views

The finding summaries use plain language and retain the values shown in the paper. During discussion, consider what might explain each pattern, when it would matter for HCI research, and what you would want to verify before relying on the output.

Results overview

Six patterns to interpret

These summaries are designed for discussion rather than as replacements for the manuscript's full analyses.

Finding 1

Human–AI differences depend strongly on the research activity

  • Interview Qualitative Study is farthest from the matched Human portrait (mean distance .495), while System Tool Implementation is closest (.169).
  • Across all activities, AI-chain is slightly farther from Human than Human-handoff (.301 versus .281).
  • The largest AI-chain shifts occur in Empirical Finding Reporting (+.077), Design Implication Development (+.066), and Controlled Experiment Design (+.052).

Each group-colored bar is the mean across all six AI configurations; the paired points retain the HH and AC values for each model family.

Finding 2

AI outputs often converge on fewer recurring category patterns

  • Across the 27 activities, normalized category entropy is .071 lower for AI than for Human outputs.
  • Twelve activities are more concentrated under AI, five are more dispersed, and ten remain unresolved by the paper-bootstrap intervals.
  • Qualitative Coding and Analysis shows the strongest concentration; Factual Description Extraction shows the largest expansion.
  • Potentially helpful: In Qualitative Coding and Analysis, 96.2% of AI outputs versus 52.1% of Human outputs are concentrated in the grounded-evidence category (70 papers).
  • Potentially harmful: In Survey Data Collection, the sampling scheme is unstated in 78.1% of AI outputs versus 12.5% of Human outputs (16 papers).
  • Descriptively neutral: In Autoethnographic Methodology, 77.3% of AI outputs versus 50.0% of Human outputs use an analytic-autoethnography approach (11 papers). This identifies an approach rather than scoring its quality.
Finding 3

Within each model family, Human-handoff and AI-chain are the closest configurations

  • The HH–AC distances are .198 for GPT, .225 for Claude, and .197 for Gemini.
  • The interactive view contains all seven global arm positions and 700 anonymized paper-by-arm points from 100 papers.

Finding 4

Models propose different research routes than the Human papers

  • Across 99 papers, model-proposed activity sets are more similar to one another (Jaccard .545–.580) than to the realized Human sets (.392–.395).
  • Model proposals more often include build-and-evaluate routes, including System Tool Implementation → Evaluation with Users (+45.5 pp).
  • Human graphs more often connect Empirical Finding Reporting → Design Implication Development (model-minus-Human: −48.8 pp).

Each matrix cell reports how much more or less often a direct dependency appears across papers.

Finding 5

Simulated-participant studies compress cohort sizes and often follow the model's own agenda

  • Across 17 activities, AI-proposed cohort sizes vary less with the Human study size (fitted slope .503).
  • Across 37 interview activities, simulated responses align more with questions produced by the same model route in 28 cases, tie in three, and align more with other routes in six.
Finding 6

AI makes more supporting detail visible, but the linked interpretation can still extend beyond it

More visible support

Evidence links in qualitative analysis increase by 42.0–47.1 pp. Status and error behavior in system implementations appears in 36.6% of AI outputs and 2.4% of Human outputs.

More overreach

Design implications extending beyond the findings rise from 17.4% in Human outputs to 37.9% across AI arms.

More visible friction

Method-linked limitations, disagreement, risks, and safeguards are 27.7 pp more common in AI outputs.

Uneven claim uptake

Visible friction leaves the linked claim unchanged or stronger in 14 of 48 AI pairs and 1 of 13 Human pairs.
